html:
A Korean Buddhist book printed in 1377 at Heungdeok Temple in Cheongju, under the Goryeo dynasty. It is the oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type, older than the Gutenberg Bible by about 78 years.

Its full title means, roughly, "Anthology of great Buddhist priests' Zen teachings". The monk Baegun gathered the sayings of Zen masters to guide students. It was printed in two volumes, but only the second survives, and not complete.

Korean printers cast bronze type using moulds, building on the long tradition of woodblock printing that also produced the Tripitaka Koreana. Earlier, in Song China, Bi Sheng had used type of baked clay.

A French diplomat in Seoul acquired the surviving volume in the late 1800s, and it is now in the National Library of France in Paris. Korea has asked for it back. UNESCO added it to the Memory of the World register in 2001.
